Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up / pilot scope

Thanks for the conversation earlier, Jasmine.

Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks before we lock the pilot:
- We want to validate responses on our production-like dataset (approx 45k monthly queries; 10k unique prompts).
- Primary success measures: response relevance (we can provide eval rubric), and acceptable latency under load.

Can you confirm: what level of isolation will the pilot run under (shared vs dedicated capacity)? Also, we'll need a simple procurement path and an SSO setup so our engineers can access the test endpoint.

I can share a sample workload and a short labeled set (10–20 examples) for early quality checks. Samantha will coordinate procurement internally.

Thanks — looking forward to a short plan and owners.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Veridian.ai
alex.johnson@veridian.ai

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot validation metrics & runbook — next steps

Alex — thanks for the call and for outlining the workloads. Per our discussion, attached is a proposed 4-week pilot plan and a short runbook. Key pieces below; please call out anything you want adjusted.

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail gating for pilot):
- Latency: p95 generation time < 650 ms (end-to-end, payload + model).
- Throughput: sustained 45 req/s with tail-latency check (no more than 5% requests > 1.2s).
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0025 under pilot traffic profile (we'll report cost breakdown).
- Quality: 80% or higher pass rate on your labeled evaluation rubric (we'll run automated evals weekly).

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (prep, 3 days): sample data upload, access/SSO exchange, baseline latency-only smoke.
- Week 1: small-scale integration (10% of target traffic), run initial relevance sweep.
- Week 2: ramp to 50% traffic, run automated quality eval and manual review.
- Week 3: full-load validation, cost & throughput profiling, run regression tests.
- Week 4: handover readout and go/no-go decision; detailed ops runbook and rollback plan delivered.

Owners / roles:
- Redwood technical lead: Jasmine Liu — integration, runbook, eval harness.
- Redwood account lead: Ben Carter — commercial/PO and SOW.
- Customer success / onboarding: Marissa Cole — runbook handoff, support triage.
- Veridian PM: Alex Johnson — sample data, evaluation rubric, internal stakeholders.

Attachments included (stubs):
- redwood_pilot_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF) — runbook + checklist
- sample_payloads.json (JSON) — masked sample queries (10k row subset)

Immediate asks for kick-off:
1) Please share the labeled evaluation rubric (CSV or simple spreadsheet) and the SSO/SP metadata for test accounts.
2) Confirm whether you prefer dedicated capacity for pilot or shared-with-fallback (we recommended dedicated for predictable tail latency).
3) Approve the success criteria above or mark items for discussion.

If those look good, Ben can coordinate a short SOW & DocuSign to make the pilot billing/procurement straightforward. Proposed kickoff window: May 4–6.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.com]

—Alex

- Dedicated uplift after pilot to reserved capacity: +25% monthly (estimate for committed throughput).
- Optional: extended retention / audit logs add-on — $2,000/mo during pilot if you need extended logs (useful for compliance checks).

Next steps to lock May 5 kickoff:
1) Samantha: send PO or purchase intent to ben.carter@redwood.com (reference deal VER-4721).
2) I will send a short SOW + DocuSign link (expected signature turnaround 48 hours). Link: https://docusign.com/REDACTED-envelope-12345
3) Jasmine & Marissa will receive SSO metadata from Alex and will provision test accounts.
4) Once SOW signed, we schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff (Jasmine lead) and provide access to the pilot endpoint.
